Created 2026-07-26 — this file had never existed despite CLAUDE.md requiring post-publish 1h/24h/7d capture, so every prior Reel and carousel shipped unmeasured. Source: Meta Business Suite > 콘텐츠 > 게시됨, account epickorsnippets (asset_id 1187482087784752), read via CDP-attached Chrome. Metric column order in the object-insights detail view: 조회수(views) / 도달(reach) or 조회계정(viewer accounts, FB) / 반응(reactions) / 시청시간(total watch time) / 팔로우(follows), then a breakdown of 좋아요(likes)/댓글(comments)/공유(shares)/저장(saves) and 평균 시청 시간(avg watch time). '--' means Meta reported no value for that format.
capture_note: Third capture. Script: .tmp/meta-read-published.py, read-only. NOTE the list-view column order is 도달 → 조회수, i.e. reach BEFORE views — the reverse of what the 2026-07-26 detail-view note above records. observations: Facebook is dead weight for this account: of 7 Facebook Reel posts measured, 5 got literally 0 or ~0 views/reach (220, 313, and 311), and only 2 (175, 312) got real numbers comparable to their Instagram counterparts. The account has 0 Facebook followers, and Facebook's own reach source breakdown shows the working posts came almost entirely from Meta's recommendation surface, not followers — so Facebook performance currently looks like a coin flip on algorithmic distribution rather than anything content-driven. Do not assume every Reel needs a meaningful Facebook cross-post plan until this pattern is better understood.

Reel vs. carousel on the same topic is mixed, not a clean win for either format: 311's Reel clearly beat its carousel (2,000 vs 972 views), but 312's carousel beat its Reel (606 vs 432) and 313's carousel beat its Reel too (880 vs 453). At this sample size (3 matched pairs), there's no evidence that Reels categorically outperform carousels — it looks topic-dependent, and 311 (Tteokbokki/food) may simply be a strong topic in either format rather than proof Reels are the better format.

Average completion rate (avg watch time / duration) has ranged 12-29% across the 7 Reels measured, with today's 175 (29%) the clear high point and 171/220 (~12%) the low point. There isn't yet a clean pattern explaining the spread by topic, hook style, or duration — worth tracking as more Reels land.

171 and 220 share the same weak-hook signature (avg completion ~12%, 0 saves) despite being produced months apart, suggesting this may be a recurring hook-writing issue for food/street-snack topics specifically, not a one-off.

175 (Namdaemun vs Dongdaemun) is the first Reel in this file to break 5 saves and 25%+ completion — worth watching its 24h/7d numbers specifically once they land, since it may represent a real format/hook improvement rather than noise.
n is still small (7 Reels, 3 carousels) and the account is freshly reactivated — treat all of the above as directional, not conclusive.

findings_2026_08_13.headline: Card news beats Reels on views, three months running, and everything is declining.
findings_2026_08_13.method_note: Median, not mean — a single 4,829-view outlier (jjimjilbang, 2026-05-29) drags every mean. Only posts aged 14 days or more are compared across months; Instagram keeps accumulating views for days, so recent posts are listed separately and NOT used for trend.
findings_2026_08_13.facebook: Effectively dead. 10 Facebook Reels average 206 views, 0 saves, 1 share total. Most rows read 0 reach. The cross-post costs nothing but should not be counted as distribution.
findings_2026_08_13.strategic_tension: Three new Reels frame designs were built on 2026-08-13 (Split Grid, Spec Sheet, Timeline) and are scheduled 8/28-30. Card news has out-viewed Reels every month measured. That does not make Reels wrong — they serve a different funnel step — but the production balance has never been checked against this number.
findings_2026_08_13.what_this_cannot_say: Whether the decline is content quality, account health, seasonality, or an Instagram distribution change. One account, one snapshot, no control. Do not attribute a cause from this table.
